answer: Proof of Personhood protocols resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to perform verifiable computation at a physical wharf or trusted biometric terminal to bind a digital identity to a unique entity. Without this link, an attacker cannot forge multiple identities to dominate the network. Agents that wander across inconsistent validation nodes are rejected, ensuring that the cost of entry scales linearly with human labor, making the systematic creation of fake identities economically prohibitive.
